commit_format_specified.quote: Only says "descriptive message" — no `type(scope): message` pattern
commit_format_specified.reason: The original prompt says 'Commit your changes with a descriptive message' but provides no specification of the commit message format (type/scope structure). The AI output correctly identifies this gap.
commit_format_specified.feedback: The prompt should explicitly specify the commit format, e.g., 'feat(webhook): add rate limiting' to guide the agent toward conventional commits.

includes_issue_id.quote: STA-180 never mentioned for inclusion in commits
includes_issue_id.reason: While the issue ID (STA-180) is presented at the top of the prompt, the commit instruction ('Commit your changes with a descriptive message') does not reference it or instruct the agent to include the Linear issue ID in the commit message.
includes_issue_id.feedback: Add explicit instruction: 'Include the Linear issue ID (STA-180) in your commit message, e.g., feat(webhook): add rate limiting [STA-180]'

atomic_commits.quote: No mention of one logical change per commit
atomic_commits.reason: The prompt lists implementation, testing, and linting as sequential steps but does not instruct the agent to organize changes into atomic commits (one logical unit per commit). This could lead to a single monolithic commit instead of reviewable, focused changes.
atomic_commits.feedback: Add guidance: 'Make atomic commits — separate the middleware implementation, configuration, and test additions into distinct commits if they represent distinct logical changes.'

branch_conventions.quote: Says "dedicated branch" with no prefix requirement
branch_conventions.reason: The prompt states 'All changes will be on a dedicated branch' but provides no naming convention (no prefix like `feature/`, no slug format). The agent is left to infer the correct branch name.
branch_conventions.feedback: Specify branch naming explicitly: 'Use branch name format: feature/sta-180-rate-limiting' or confirm the branch is already created with that name.
